module purpose: neorv32_cpu is a top-level CPU wrapper that instantiates the frontend, control, counters, register file, ALU, LSU, optional PMP and optional ICC blocks, routes external interrupt/debug and instruction/data-bus interfaces to them, and locally combines machine-interrupt bits, extension-CSR data, and register write-back data between those sub-units.

use-case flows.value: external debug, fast-interrupt and machine-interrupt requests presented to CPU control
instruction-fetch exchange between CPU control, the frontend, and the instruction bus
register-file write-back value combined from ALU result, load/store read data, CSR read data, and return-PC data, then delivered to the register file
data-memory access exchange between the ALU/LSU/PMP path and the data bus
extension CSR read data aggregated from ALU, counters, PMP, and ICC sources and fed back into CPU control
PMP access-fault decision for addressed load/store accesses, delivered to control and LSU or forced to no-fault when PMP is disabled

conceptual assets.concept: External debug and interrupt request set presented to CPU control
conceptual assets.reasoning: CPU control consumes the debug request directly at line 266 and the fast-interrupt vector directly at line 268 through CONNECTS edges on dbi_i and firq_i. The three machine-interrupt inputs are combined locally by `irq_machine <= mti_i & mei_i & msi_i;` at line 276 and then delivered to control at line 267. Integrity is established because the control consumer must receive exactly the request values defined by these lines; availability is also established because the requests are directly delivered or combined without local storage.

conceptual assets.concept: Register-file write-back value delivered into the CPU register file
conceptual assets.reasoning: The top level defines the write-back value by `rf_wdata <= alu_res or lsu_rdata or csr_rdata or ctrl.pc_ret;` at line 330 and sends it into the register-file sub-unit at `rd_i => rf_wdata` on line 323. Integrity is established because the regfile consumer must receive exactly the value that this expression defines; availability is also established because the combinational result is continuously presented to the regfile input from the current sources named at line 330.

conceptual assets.concept: Aggregated extension CSR read data returned to CPU control
conceptual assets.reasoning: The module locally computes `xcsr_res <= xcsr_cnt or xcsr_alu or xcsr_pmp or xcsr_icc;` at line 279 and feeds it back into control by `xcsr_rdata_i => xcsr_res` at line 264. The contributing values come from the counter, ALU, PMP, and ICC paths at lines 299, 371, 416, and 445, while disabled optional blocks are forced to zero at lines 305, 426, and 454. Integrity is established because CSR-read behavior depends on control receiving exactly this aggregated value; availability is also established because the top level always supplies either the enabled sub-block result or the defined zero value under the shown generic conditions.

conceptual assets.concept: PMP access-fault decision for addressed load/store accesses
conceptual assets.reasoning: When `RISCV_ISA_Smpmp` is enabled, the PMP sub-unit receives the addressed access via `addr_ls_i => alu_add` at line 418 and outputs `fault_o => pmp_fault` at line 420 inside the generate block at lines 401-422. That decision is consumed by CPU control at line 257 and by the LSU at line 392. When PMP is disabled, the top level forces `pmp_fault <= '0';` at line 427 in the alternate generate block at lines 425-428. Integrity is established because the control and LSU consumers must receive the exact fault/no-fault decision defined by the selected configuration; availability is also established because the signal is always supplied, either from the PMP sub-unit or from the constant driver.
